rootCauseOneLine: timelineWindowEventBudget bounds synchronous timeline builds by a fixed event count justified by a one-host "0.06ms/event" figure, but build cost is CPU- and payload-byte-dependent (SQLite read + JSON.parse ~80%), so on slow hosts a full 1500-event window blocks the event loop far longer than the ~100ms the constant promises; the existing 4 MiB byte cut is not operator-tunable and never engages for latency.

prReviews.topFinding: Docs-only; bakes one VPS's unverifiable and selection-biased numbers (derived only from >=150ms slow-build log lines) into the shared feature-flags.ts JSDoc, and the configuration.md recipe omits that the log samples only the slow tail and that a whole finished turn is always returned even above the budget; does not touch the real lever (the existing byte-based window cut).

proposedFix: Promote the existing THREAD_TIMELINE_EVENT_DATA_BYTE_LIMIT (4 MiB, applyTimelineWindowByteBudget / findStoredTimelineWindowByteBudgetFloor) to a feature flag timelineWindowByteBudget (BB_FF_TIMELINE_WINDOW_BYTE_BUDGET) threaded like eventBudget, default ~1.5 MiB with 4 MiB kept as the memory clamp; document both knobs (configuration.md, guide template, bb-cli skill) and reword the source comment to say the count is a hardware/payload-dependent proxy. Avoid runtime calibration unless the timeline cache and latest-rows keys also include the effective budget. Structural fix (out of scope): incremental projection or moving the build off the event loop.
caveats: Could not measure on the reporter's 4-core VPS; hardware dependence was demonstrated by CPU-throttling the same test (~4x cost, 124.5ms > 100ms for a full window) rather than on real slow hardware. On this Ryzen 7 workstation the constant is conservative (0.024 ms/event). The reporter's 0.479 ms/event p50 is a slow-tail estimate because the log line only fires for builds >= 150ms. Nothing on origin/main after the base commit changes this code. No dev instance or provider turns were needed.
